R implementation of generateGLVparmsFromAdj

Source: R/generateGLVparms.R
generateGLVparmsFromAdjR.Rd

Generates random parameters of a generalized Lotka-Volterra model from an adjacency matrix. It is equivalent to generateGLVparmsFromAdj(): it has the same arguments and, for the same random seed, it gives the same results (this is checked by the package tests). It is written in R, so it is slower but easier to read and modify, and it can be used as a reference implementation. See generateGLVparmsFromAdj() for a detailed description of how the parameters are generated.

Usage

generateGLVparmsFromAdjR(
  adjM,
  ef,
  predIntAvg = 0.01,
  selfLimAvg = c(0.01, 0.01, 0.01),
  migrAvg = 0,
  preserveInt = 0,
  predIntSd = 0.01,
  rndType = 0
)

Arguments

adjM

Numeric square matrix with the structure of the interactions. Only the signs and the zeros are used when preserveInt = 0; with preserveInt 1 or 2 the values of the non-zero off-diagonal entries are used as well.

ef

Efficiency of predator-prey interactions: effect on the predator / effect on the prey.

predIntAvg

Average strength of the interactions (predator-prey, competition and mutualism) when preserveInt = 0.

selfLimAvg

Numeric vector of length 3 with the average self-limitation of 1 = mutualistic, 2 = basal and 3 = consumer species (diagonal entries of the interaction matrix).

migrAvg

Average migration rate, the migration of each species is uniform in [0, 2 * migrAvg].

preserveInt

How to define the strength of the interactions:

  • 0: random values defined by rndType with mean predIntAvg.

  • 1: the values of adjM are preserved (off-diagonal entries only).

  • 2: random uniform values with mean given by the value in adjM for each interaction, that is, uniform in [0, 2 * abs(adjM[i, j])].

predIntSd

Standard deviation of the strengths when preserveInt = 0 and rndType = 1 (gamma distribution). For the uniform distribution the sd is fixed at predIntAvg * 2 / sqrt(12).

rndType

Distribution of the strengths when preserveInt = 0: 0 = uniform, 1 = gamma. Other values of preserveInt always use the uniform distribution.

Value

A list with the interaction matrix interM (with the self-limitation in the diagonal), the intrinsic growth rates r and the migration rates m. They can be passed to metaWebNetAssemblyGLV() as metaW, r and m.

See also

generateGLVparmsFromAdj() for the Rcpp implementation, generateRandomGLVadjMat() to generate adjM, and metaWebNetAssemblyGLV().

Examples

set.seed(1)
adj <- generateRandomGLVadjMat(20, 0.2, c(0.1, 0.3, 0.3, 0.15, 0.15))
set.seed(2)
a <- generateGLVparmsFromAdj(adj, ef = 0.1)
set.seed(2)
b <- generateGLVparmsFromAdjR(adj, ef = 0.1)
all.equal(a, b)
#> [1] TRUE
